title.narrative: ROAF/ETH/Preparation of ten regional development spatial plans in the regions of Tigray, Afar, Amhara, Oromia, Somali, Gambella, Harari, Benishangul Gumuz, Sidama and SNNP

description.narrative: The Ministry of Urban Development and Construction (MUDCo) has embarked on an ambitious technical assistance program on regional planning to conduct studies on the development schemes of ten regions in Ethiopia. This project intends to prepare ten regional development spatial plans, which each comprises of land use and regional infrastructure network schemes with various appropriate scales, investment priorities per the comparative and competitive advantage, relevant regional development programs (i.e., policy and development programs/projects) and implementation plan. This UN-Habitat Technical Assistance on Regional Development spatial Planning project was proposed by the Agency in 2018 and later extended in April 2020 at the request of MUDCo. The Terms of Reference for the project aims to formulate Regional Development Spatial Plans (RDSPs) for all ten regional states, including Tigray, Afar, Amhara, Oromia, Somali, Benishangul Gumuz, SNNP, Gambella, Harari, and Sidama, that bring about balanced territorial (urban and rural) development and support regional governments prioritize investments. Moreover, the Plans aim to create functional rural-urban and urban-urban integrations and complementarities between the same in promoting an overall rapid socio-economic development in the region by making urban centers as engines of growth and transformation. By unlocking the resource potential of regions and territories, RDSP emphasizes minimizing regional inequalities and hence bringing about balanced development. This could lead to reduced internal migration, minimized conflicts, and enhanced peace in the country. The UN-Habitat understands that it is crucial to establish an all-inclusive regional development planning system that focuses on the spatial distribution of the regions’ economic and social developments to provide an effective link between the planning processes of the economic development and infrastructure and to achieve the implementation of overall development goals of the country, the efficient utilization of regional resources, the reduction of unwanted impacts of constraints on development, the exploitation of potentials and opportunities for sustainable regional growth, and which builds on established institutional and legal frameworks for the preparation and operationalization of the regional development plans. This project was developed through a series of assessments of literature and consultations in 2019/20 with partners and stakeholders at different levels of government in Addis Ababa, Jigjiga (Somali Regional State), Hawassa (SNNPR), and Bahir Dar (Amhara Regional State). This proposal was developed jointly with the main partner at MUDCo, the Bureau of Urban Plan Preparation and Implementation follow-up (BUPPIF), and its affiliate -- the Urban Revenue Enhancement, Fund Mobilization, and Finance Bureau. Through the assessments, numerous common topics surfaced, the most notable of which are: (i) reform of regional institutions with a focus on capacity development of core processes that enhance leadership and management capabilities, adoption of good governance practices and updating strategic development plans through improved working systems and human resource development; (ii) progress in the decentralization agenda through economic development and civic engagement in planning, implementation and decision making processes by ensuring community mobilization and involvement of stakeholders including marginalized groups ( women, children and youth); and (iii) institutionalization of appropriate regional development strategies including quantifying and qualifying social, economic and environmental parameters of sustainable livelihood. The country’s Ten-year Perspective Plan illustrates, in its urban and regional components, strategies on how to strengthen regional and local governments and administrative institutions, the need to invest in network infrastructures, ensure economic transformation, integrate urban, rural and peri-urban systems, harmonize various planning levels, and methods to improve financing mechanisms. The development strategies also present and discuss mechanisms to improve governance and deepen decentralization; mainstreaming community participation in integrated urban and regional planning; designing of workable policy based on assessed needs; improving urban and rural basic functions and services; and standardizing core business processes are key intended outcomes of this project. The project mainly aims to prepare regional development spatial plans for the regional states of Tigray, Afar, Amhara, Oromia, Somali, Benishangul Gumuz, Southern Nations, Nationalities and People (SNNP), Gambella, Harari and Sidama that can enable them to define and achieve their own development goals in a manner that contribute to the achievement of the national development goals.
